articles.title: Bunker review – Cruz and Bardem just can’t dig Florian Zeller’s shallow thriller out of a hole
articles.summary: Venice film festival: An architect (Javier Bardem) alienates his book editor wife (Penélope Cruz) when he agrees to build a luxurious bunker for a tech billionaire. Even the formidable pairing of Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem can’t save this new movie from writer-director Florian Zeller – his…
body: Bunker has nothing that interesting or original to say about its metaphorically showcased theme of alienation and inequality; the central relationship is left unexplored in favour of so-so home-invasion suspense styling – although one extended marital-argument scene showed what might have been achieved if their relationship was the film’s point – and the violent finale ending is outrageously glib, silly and unconvincing. An off-camera paramedic or doctor actually has to be heard explaining in a brief sentence afterwards what is supposed to have happened. Very lame.

Cruz and Bardem are Sofia and Miguel, a stylish Spanish couple with two teen daughters; the family has moved to London so that Sofia, a book editor, can take up a job managing a UK publisher’s foreign literature in translation list.

Miguel is a world-famous architect (what other sort is there?) who cordially tells an interviewer that he can work in any city. It seems as if he might himself have designed the huge, modernist rear extension to their handsome Victorian terrace house.

articles.title: Elon Musk told ex-girlfriend he needed ‘a legion of children before the civil war’
articles.summary: Ashley St Clair was speaking at the Venice film premiere of Alex Gibney’s documentary Musk, where she warned of his dangerous influence. • Musk review – epic study of the world’s richest and most banal man.
body: Elon Musk is sowing “deliberate division” via his social media platform X that will be catastrophic unless regulated, the mother of one of the 14 confirmed children fathered by the world’s richest man has warned.

In Musk, a new documentary by veteran film-maker Alex Gibney, former Maga influencer Ashley St Clair says Musk told her in a text message he wanted to have a child with her because he needed to have “a legion of children before the civil war”.

The couple had a son in 2024 but have since separated. St Clair says Musk’s team offered her a $40m lump-sum payment and a monthly stipend of $100,000 in return for her signing a non-disclosure agreement but withdrew the offer after she refused to sign it.

Asked at the documentary’s Venice film festival premiere whether her ex-partner was just scared of a civil war or actively trying to stoke one, St Clair said: “Whatever it is, what he’s doing with this platform on X cannot be ignored, because he is stoking flames that don’t exist in the real world.”

articles.title: State handouts, 10,000 lasers – and Trump’s election: six things we learned from the Elon Musk film
articles.summary: Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children.
body: Veteran documentarian Alex Gibney’s film about the richest broligarch on the planet has been one of the most eagerly anticipated films at the Venice film festival this year. The Oscar-winning 72-year-old, who has in previous films taken on the US military, the Catholic church, Vladimir Putin and Scientology, has been investigating the tech tycoon’s ascent and speaking to people in his orbit since late 2022, before his Maga turn and Trump 2.0.

Recently, Musk has held forth at length about his view that “suicidal empathy” – people who have more empathy for criminals than the victims of criminals, in his view – is behind the decline of western civilisation. Empathy isn’t bad, he says in the doc, it’s just that it’s become too shallow. But interviews in the film raise the question of whether Musk is capable of empathy at all. This is a man who tells his wife that “if you were my employee, I would fire you”, and urges her to tell his estranged trans-daughter Jenna that “I’ll always love her” – and then cuts off her health insurance the next day.
points: Alex Gibney’s marathon documentary delivers numerous eye-raising insights into the broligarch’s business deals, early idealism and apocalyptic appetite for fathering children.

articles.title: ‘Drunk History’ Returns With New Short-Form Episodes 7 Years After Comedy Central Finale
articles.summary: After a long hangover, “Drunk History” is back. The Emmy-winning comedy show is returning with three new short-form episodes, seven years after it last aired on Comedy Central. From Derek Waters and Jeremy Konner, “Drunk History” pairs inebriated storytellers with scrappy historical reenactments.
body: The other storylines center on Frances Perkins (the unsung architect of FDR’s New Deal) and two men’s lifelong battle to make the world’s largest ball of twine.

“Drunk History” started in 2007 as a Funny or Die web series before Comedy Central picked it up as a TV show that ran for six seasons from 2013 to 2019. That year, the network renewed “Drunk History” for a seventh season but reversed the decision in 2020, when production was halted due to the pandemic.
Guest stars over the years include Jack Black, Will Ferrell, Bill Hader, Kristen Wiig, Lin-Manuel Miranda, Bob Odenkirk and more.
“I’m so excited to be back making Drunk History again! We have a lot of catching up to do,” said Waters.

articles.title: Musk review – epic study of the world’s richest and most banal man
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Alex Gibney interviews former colleagues, wives, the trillionaire’s father and a CG avatar in this absorbing documentary. ‘Elon is a nuke.” The speaker is Ashley St Clair, a former conservative Maga influencer and one of Elon Musk’s former girlfriends-slash-baby mommas.
body: She is a fascinating expert witness in Alex Gibney’s four-hour epic study of the world’s richest and dullest man: the overgrown brattish South-African-born trillionaire plutocrat, ersatz visionary and Trump courtier who owns Tesla cars, SpaceX rocket ships, Starlink satellites on which nation states’ military capabilities are increasingly reliant, X (formerly Twitter) which shapes the collective “incel” id of billions and GrokAI whose vast server farms daily guzzle oceans of precious water.

As head of Trump’s incompetent cost-cutting Doge (Department of Government Efficiency) unit, Musk actually increased the US deficit by sacking thousands of revenue officers whose job was to rake in tax – while reportedly accessing and improperly sharing Americans’ sensitive social security data.
He does indeed look like a nuke, efficiently designed, destructive, seemingly unguided and uncontrolled.

Gibney’s excellent film covers a lot of ground in its extraordinary story, although we don’t get to hear about the mysterious process that changed a balding youngster into a follicularly unchallenged mature man.

articles.title: Netflix to Report Box Office Numbers for 6 Upcoming Movies as Streamer Escalates Theatrical Plans (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “La Bola Negra” has mucho heat. The generational queer drama swept the Cannes Film Festival off its feet in May, nabbing a $5 million sale to Netflix and earning helmers Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo the jury prize for best director.
body: “The real question is ‘What does Netflix want to be now?’” posed one high-level executive at a legacy film studio. “Having almost bought Warner Bros. Discovery, you get the sense that they can’t put some of that toothpaste back in the tube.”

The cinema owners, in turn, have done their share of resisting Netflix titles, namely over the company’s refusal to give them a standard period of exclusivity before moving to streaming. COVID- 19 dashed all theatrical hopes when cineplexes were shut down, and the exhibitors have been clawing their way back to normalcy (playing films for 45 days on the big screen before moving them to other windows is the current industry standard). For one of the most deep-pocketed tech monoliths in the world to reconsider, even lightly, its position on theatrical would be a boost, one veteran film distributor says.

articles.title: Danielle Deadwyler, Ike Barinholtz and Connor Storrie Join Billie Eilish and Carey Mulligan in ‘The Bell Jar’
articles.summary: Focus Features has confirmed the cast for Academy Award winner Sarah Polley‘s “The Bell Jar,” starring Billie Eilish. Eilish, a two-time Oscar-winning singer-songwriter, makes her film acting debut playing Esther Greenwood, the protagonist of Sylvia Plath’s classic novel.
body: Also confirmed to star are Gotham Award winner Danielle Deadwyler as Dr. Nolan, Esther’s psychiatrist; Actor Award winner Ike Barinholtz as Lenny, a wealthy NYC radio host; and “Heated Rivalry” breakout Connor Storrie as Marco, whom Esther is set up with on a horrifying blind date. Dylan Hawco (as Buddy Willard, Esther’s first boyfriend), Lili Taylor (Jay Cee, editor of Ladies’ Day magazine), Ella Beatty (Joan, an old acquaintance who ends up at the same mental hospital as Esther) and Maggie Kuntz (Doreen, Esther’s best friend in New York and a fellow intern) are also featured in the ensemble cast.
“The Bell Jar” is produced by Plan B, Studiocanal and Joy Coalition. Focus will distribute the film, with a release date to be announced.
Polley is represented by WME, GGA, and Circle Management + Production and Eilish is represented by WME, Sandbox Entertainment, High Rise PR and Gang, Tyre, Ramer, Brown & Passman, Inc.

articles.title: Glastonbury confirms ticket sale dates - and highest ever price
articles.summary: The festival will return in June after taking a fallow year, but tickets have topped £400 for the first time.
body: After taking a fallow year in 2026, the Glastonbury Festival has confirmed that tickets for next year's event will go on sale in October.
Tickets for the weekend will cost £408 including a £5 booking fee per ticket - an increase of £29.50 from 2025.

Headliners for the festival, which takes place from 23 to 27 June, have yet to be announced, but rumours are already swirling, with everyone from Harry Styles and Fontaines DC to Taylor Swift and Stevie Wonder said to be in the mix.
Tickets for the festival typically sell out in less than an hour, with thousands of fans joining online queues to fight for their place.

articles.title: ‘Snowfall’ Spinoff ‘The Drop’ Is an Evocative, If Uneven, Portrait of South L.A. in the Gangsta Rap Era: TV Review
articles.summary: The FX drama “Snowfall” was one of the sneak success stories of the Peak TV era. Co-created by a marquee film director in “Boyz N the Hood” auteur John Singleton, “Snowfall” thrived where many series of similar origin failed.
body: While “The Drop” doesn’t craft its protagonists into figures as compelling as Dr. Dre, Ice Cube or Snoop Dogg, the world they navigate is instilled with a vivid sense of place. It’s rare for productions to film in L.A. these days, let alone celebrate the city to the extent “The Drop” does. That’s a quality worth admiring, even if the series can be uneven in its early episodes.
“The Drop” premieres on FX and Hulu on Sep. 8 at 9pm ET, with remaining episodes airing weekly on Tuesdays.

articles.title: Oasis' Cardiff reunion gig was 'hugely emotional' say film-makers
articles.summary: Filmmakers describe the gig as a "hugely emotional" experience that took Noel Gallagher by surprise.
body: Will Lovelace and Dylan Southern's portrayal of the band's world tour in 2025 also captured the moment Liam and Noel reunited in the rehearsal studios following a 15-year hiatus.
Reflecting on the opening gig, Southern said: "You saw grown men who probably rarely express their emotions crying and hugging each other.
"Noel says in the film that he completely underestimated what it would be like, and it really did kind of hit him hard."
Lovelace said: "Those opening few moments, just as they're about to go on stage in Cardiff, and then the first song, was definitely a turning point on the tour but certainly in the film."

articles.title: 'I didn't want to leave The Voice', says Sir Tom Jones
articles.summary: The Welsh singer has appeared as an on-off coach on the competition since it premiered in 2012.
body: Sir Tom Jones has said ITV "fired" him as a judge on The Voice, and he did not want to leave as he "loves the show".
The 86-year-old singer from Treforest in Pontypridd, Rhondda Cynon Taf, has appeared as an on-off coach on the singing competition since it premiered in 2012.
Following rumours that he may not return to the panel for the upcoming series, Sir Tom said the broadcaster decided a while ago, but he "was told recently".
He said on social media that he had been offered a reduced role - one he was "not thrilled" about.
